title: Review unused generic flexibility
why: A private generic used with only one concrete type carries abstraction and monomorphization cost without providing current variation.
suggestion: Use the concrete type until another real caller requires generic behavior, or document the external contract that needs the type parameter.
limitations: Requires exactly one used type parameter, at least two visible explicit type applications, one identical concrete type, a unique declaration name, and no unresolved bare references.

Rust public and contract functions are excluded. Type arguments mentioning parameters bound by a lexically enclosing function, impl, trait, struct, or enum are not treated as concrete; generic names in unrelated scopes do not exclude calls. C++ support is limited to static definitions in source files, excluding headers.

Inferred type arguments, macro expansion, aliases, overloads, external consumers, compile-time impact, and profile-guided hot-path cost are not inferred. Rust generic binders are recognized lexically in masked source, including visible impl binders in macro bodies; complex const-generic headers and qualified paths sharing a generic parameter name can remain conservative unknowns.
